dependency: The preferred operating dependency is the operator belief that sustained 70% vibration is necessary to prevent low doses, followed by increased vibration when flow drops. The supplied fixed-schedule traces do not establish that necessity or observe the proposed operator-response feedback. The causal_return_path_hypothesis is that strong vibration promotes outlet redistribution or packing, slower discharge elicits more strong vibration, and that return increases obstruction. It remains a hypothesis: neither packing, pressure nor band composition was measured.

predictions.account: Forward harmful-return hypothesis: strong vibration contributes to outlet packing or segregation, and renewed strong vibration perpetuates low flow.
predictions.result: Hypothesis: after an identical initial 70% window, substituting locked 30% vibration in windows 2-4 will produce fewer no-flow intervals and smaller dose errors than continued 70%, possibly with less band persistence. Recovery would support a harmful amplitude contribution without proving packing or segregation. Failure to recover could reflect persistent first-window damage or another mechanism.
predictions.when: Compare proposed fresh-charge trials T2 and T3 at the same window boundaries, accounting for recorded fill height and accumulated discharge. T2 uses 70% for the first four 15-second windows and 0 for the fifth. T3 uses 70% in window 1, then 30% in windows 2-4 and 0 in window 5; do not escalate when doses or flow fall. Both energize for exactly 60 seconds. This intervenes on the hypothesized strong-vibration return link while fixing the initial 300 g charge, composition, first-window drive, geometry, 25 +/- 2 g demand and five-window outcome criterion.

predictions.account: Reversed causal arrow: declining fill height, moisture or a pre-existing outlet restriction causes low flow, which prompts the operator to choose stronger vibration; stronger vibration is a response and may be neutral or helpful.
predictions.result: Hypothesis: if stronger vibration is only a response, continued 70% should not systematically worsen later flow relative to T3 at comparable recorded fill conditions; reducing the setting could leave low doses unchanged or worsen them. If low flow precedes the proposed response, that temporal order favors the reversed arrow but does not exclude feedback. The already stipulated exogenous fixed-schedule 70% versus 30% anomaly challenges a pure response-only account, but one trace per setting cannot identify its cause.
predictions.when: Use the same T2/T3 comparison, with camera timing of no-flow onset and predetermined switch times. The schedules are precommitted rather than triggered by flow, so they test the drive-to-flow arrow without making poor flow the cause of stronger drive. Recorded height is contextual evidence, not an independently controlled variable; actual operator escalation is not present in the supplied traces.

predictions.account: Alternative reversible restriction hypothesis: an outlet obstruction can relax after a mechanical disturbance, independently of a strong-vibration feedback mechanism.
predictions.result: Hypothesis: one specified external tap will improve subsequent flow relative to the replicated 30% schedule if a reversible restriction is limiting discharge. Recovery would support mechanical reversibility, without establishing compaction, band composition or the feedback loop; no recovery would not exclude an obstruction.
predictions.when: T1 replicates 30% for windows 1-4, then 0 for window 5. T4 repeats that schedule on a fresh charge with exactly one measured 5 mm downward external mount tap during the 10-second off interval after window 3. Compare windows 4-5, separating any pre-tap differences. Across T1-T4 use four fresh 300 g charges, five 15-second windows with four 10-second off gaps, identical cup exchanges while off, closed containment and unchanged geometry. No trial exceeds 60 energized seconds within 120 seconds; a duty violation invalidates it.

surviving_outcome: The valued outcome remains 25 +/- 2 g per 15-second window for five successive windows through the existing outlet in this fictional enclosed bench scenario. Useful partial success would be fewer low-dose windows or a narrower spread with an explicit fill-range limit. These outcomes remain targets, not demonstrated intervention results. The stipulated 30% comparison gives 24, 23, 21, 19 and 5 g: two windows meet tolerance, versus one in the 70% trace of 26, 20, 17, 15 and 4 g. Thus some acceptable dosing is observed without 70%, challenging universal necessity, while five-window sufficiency is unproved. Neither observed trace attains the complete target.
unknowns: The cause of declining dose is unknown: packing, segregation, moisture, fill height and other mechanisms remain candidates. The visible pale band is not an assayed composition or a measurement of packing.

The operator escalation and causal return link are hypothesized, not observed in these fixed-schedule traces. Necessity of sustained 70% for the full target is unsupported; failure of a tested alternative would not prove universal necessity.

Only four fresh-charge trials are available. Randomizing their execution order is a proposed control, but the unequal schedules lack replicated comparisons and cannot establish reliability or isolate all batch and timing effects.

Fill height after window 1 may diverge as discharge diverges; identical initial charge does not hold later height fixed. A T2/T3 difference can challenge the amplitude account but cannot uniquely establish outlet packing or exclude height-mediated effects.

No pressure transducer, composition assay or calibrated acceleration sensor is available. Nominal drive setting is not a measured particle-scale force. Record each dose and absolute target error, in-tolerance window count, cumulative mass, no-flow intervals of at least one second, band location, fill height, switch and tap times, and energized seconds.

Feasibility at all five declining fill heights within the duty limit remains unknown. The fifth window is unenergized in the proposed equal-time comparisons; its low dose cannot establish failure of every admissible redistribution of the 60-second vibration budget.

All facts are synthetic stipulations, and proposed interventions and predictions are hypotheses. The enclosed batch scenario establishes no real hardware access, physical benefit, production performance or generalization to other materials or long-term operation.
